checks: An affine positive scale times a fixed simplex gives a compact convex bundle with interior. The lattice diamond permits only z_1=0,±1, and the extreme cases force z_2=0. Thus the exact census, affine fiber-volume roots and M>4b^d follow.

Apply the paired centroid-tail fact to each reflected column pair and at zero shift to the central copy. Since b>2κ>2d/(d+1), the centroid simplex identity gives −aT⊂bT. Reflection then pays a^d at the horizontal endpoints for each continuous direction, with null overlap of the two trace boundaries. Pure-base caps capture the source and at least one whole member of each pair.

The canonical caps capture the whole left endpoint, have exact middle and column fraction γ, and strictly miss the right endpoint. They cover all column and left points. The explicit ±3 exposing tilts isolate the endpoint canonical caps and bound their depths strictly below Q, so global maximum is Q.
The primitive line residuals are (0,κ,b) and b/2>κ; changing the z_1 tilt fixes the entire column, explaining why the one-integer step argument does not apply.

Bernoulli verifies the uniform rational choice. Direct fractions verify the planar Q=104/25, M=293/25 and 144>125. The normalized inequality follows from 2N+1>3b^d and the displayed exact expression for 4Q−γM.
